title: Wolf and Garden Anew
premise: Wren Kavanagh's careful ledgers hide a dangerous truth: the Guild of Impossible Things has been quietly hoarding fragments of a sealed god, and the dying stranger's map leads to the last fragment — buried beneath the temple where Wren was raised as a debt-orphan. Hunted by the Guild's enforcers and shadowed by a wolf-souled outcast named Sable who claims the stranger was her kin, Wren must choose between the only family he's ever known and the truth the ledgers reveal: his own debt was purchased with the god's stolen name. When the Guild moves to complete the seal and erase every witness, Wren and Sable rally the temple's forgotten orphans, expose the ledgers to the city, and shatter the seal — not to free the god, but to finally let it die, ending the ancient war's last ember and winning Wren a family built on truth instead of debt.
about_author: August Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild records in a coastal city before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paper-trails, debts, and the quiet people who keep the world's secrets.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. We meet Wren balancing the Guild's impossible accounts, showing his precision, his debt-bond, and his longing for the temple that raised him. A stranger with a wolf-tooth pendant watches him across the counting-house. Emotional beat: quiet suffocation — a life measured to the copper, wanting more.

chapters.title: Blood on the Balance Sheet
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The stranger dies in the scriptorium's doorway, pressing a bloodstained map and a wax-sealed name into Wren's hands. Guild enforcers arrive minutes behind. Wren lies for the first time in his life — and realizes the lie felt like freedom. Emotional beat: terror mixed with a dangerous thrill of choice.

chapters.title: Sable at the Gate
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A wolf-souled outcast corners Wren outside the temple walls; the dead man was her brother, and the map was hers by right. She spares Wren when she sees he carries the name unknowing — and that the Guild has marked him. Emotional beat: wary alliance forged from shared grief.

chapters.title: What the Temple Buried
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Following the map beneath his childhood temple, Wren discovers the orphan-debt records: his bond was bought with a fragment of the sealed god's true name. Mother Superior Vess, his beloved mentor, knew all along. Emotional beat: betrayal cracking the foundation of belonging.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon Rises
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable teaches Wren the old roads as the Guild's hunters close in; the moon's thirteenth turn approaches, the night the seal weakens. They learn the Guild intends to complete the seal using Wren's ledger-name as the final key. Emotional beat: growing trust, and the first taste of loyalty freely given.

chapters.title: A Price Written Twice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Captured by the Guild's master of accounts, Wren is offered erasure of his debt in exchange for the map and silence. He sees the Guild's logic — the seal holds an ancient war at bay — and nearly yields. Emotional beat: the seductive comfort of a lie that would keep everyone safe.

chapters.title: The Orphans' Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Wren escapes with Sable's help and turns his skill to rebellion: copying the debt-records and god-fragments for every temple orphan the Guild has bound. The forgotten children of the city become his found family. Emotional beat: purpose kindled — from scribe of secrets to scribe of truth.

chapters.title: Night of the Turning Moon
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Guild begins the sealing rite beneath the temple as the thirteenth moon crests. Wren and the orphans infiltrate the rite; Vess must choose between her order and her ward, and chooses Wren at the cost of her rank. Emotional beat: desperate courage, family assembled from the discarded.

chapters.title: The God Who Wanted to Rest
chapters.summary: Wren and Sable, alternating POV. At the seal's heart, Wren speaks the god's true name — not to bind or free it, but to grant it the death it has begged for across centuries. The Guild's master resists; Sable takes a wound shielding Wren; the seal shatters into harmless light. Emotional beat: the climax — mercy as the bravest act.

chapters.title: Wolf and Garden Anew
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The war's ember dies with the god; the Guild falls to the published ledgers, and the debt-bonds burn. Wren, Sable, Vess, and the orphans plant a garden over the old seal-chamber — a temple of their own making. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not owed; a family written in truth.
